encyclopedia.summary: Michael Mann's 1995 crime film, a reworking of his own 1989 TV movie L.A. Takedown. Neil McCauley runs a crew of robbers, Vincent Hanna is the detective hunting him, and the two come to recognise that they live by the same rules as they close in on each other across Los Angeles. Its staging of surveillance and gunfire is still quoted by later crime films.

key_facts.value: His own TV movie L.A. Takedown (1989)

highlights: The hunter and the hunted living by the same rules is the spine of the film.
The downtown shootout used recorded real gunfire to keep the echo of the streets.
One diner scene between the two leads explains the whole film's tension.

related.note: Another film that pushes the undercover-and-chase structure hard

encyclopedia.summary: Directed by Carol Reed from a Graham Greene screenplay in 1949, the film is set in divided postwar Vienna. An American writer digs into a friend's death and finds a black market in counterfeit medicine. Famous for its tilted frames, sewer chase and zither score, it treats the city itself as the lead.
highlights: Shoots the ruins and sewers of occupied Vienna on location, leaving the city's unease on screen.
Its tilted angles keep reminding you that the characters have lost their moral footing.
The final sewer chase and the underground sequences became a standard for thrillers.
